ANC Moment of Truth

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The ANC leadership race is coming to a fever pitch this December, at stake is the position of party president and the highest office in the land.

Unique Selling Point:
News style, high paced reflection of developments concerning the ANC and its leadership issues, throwing forward to the possible outcomes of the December Elective Conference.

Summary:
It's the 55th ANC conference, a moment the party will recon with its own promises of unity and self-correcting. Marred by reports of corruption and divisive factionalism, the ruling party is going into its elective conference a shadow of itself. After suffering serious losses at the polls, a decreasing majority in parliament, navigating a 'step-aside' rule that has ostracised popular senior leaders, the party will be contending with serious issues but top priority will be presidential post. A race between the incumbent and disgraced former health minister presents a pivotal moment for the party and the country.

Script:


The African National Congress is full of bold promises.
President Cyril Ramaphosa

‘With the help of Fiona and other comrades, we are going to build her a brand new house.”
After the so-called 10 wasted years, it promised better service delivery, to rebuild the economy, root out corruption and self correct.


President Cyril Ramaphosa
“Amandla!....Amandla”

It’s a long to do list in its renewal project.

As the party gears up for its 55th national Elective Conference. Its position as the leader of society has never been more precarious.


Susan Boysen

In ways where it matters, sustaining the trust of the general South African population. It is very weak in that respect

Professor Susan Boysen is a researcher, analyst and author. For her, the party’s first task will be to revamp itself. Building on the sentiments of the step-aside rule which requires members facing criminal charges to step away from their organizational roles.

Susan Boysen

It helped create an aura of this is the end of total lack of accountability for wrongdoing

After a year of canvasing branches, two names go head to head, vying for the position of party president.

00:16
‘When we joined the ANC, the reward was not a tender, the reward was not a position as a counselor, MP or a minister,
Zweli Mkhize, always one of the favourites for the party presidency, is facing serious allegations of fraud and corruption in the R150 million Digital Vibes tender scandal, first investigated by the Daily Maverick.

Susan Boysen

he's going into this election working on the campaign, that this is a political campaign against him. We know that actually Mkhize argues that the SIU, reached their conclusions prematurely


Mkhize rejects the allegations.

But he isn’t the only one with serious allegations to answer for…

In 2020, millions in foreign currency were stolen from president Cyril Ramaphosa’s private game farm.


Now the president faces a criminal charge for allegedly not reporting the theft.

Ramaphosa has also denied that keeping the cash in his home was akin to money laundering.



It’s a scandal that has tarnished Ramaphosa’s name and standing in the party.

Zweli Mkhize

02:46 – Let me categorically state that I have not personally benefitted from this contract.





President Cyril Ramaphosa


In my book honourable speaker, it was reporting a crime to the police when I did inform a police general.

Susan B
19:38 -
The fact that there has been so much beating around the bush on the Phal phala allegations. The fact that he's not just stepped up and made a very clear cut answer, I think that's really impacting his campaign in a big way.


This week, the panel of independent experts appointed to determined whether the president has a criminal case to answer to, will hand over it’s findings to Parliament.

Once a criminal investigation gets underway, President Ramaphosa would be forced to step-aside from his duties as as leader of the ANC and this could potentially see him ousted from his office as president of the country.


and that could make 2024's general election the most uncertain yet
